memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment, medium conviction, with no capital deployed and no portfolio slot committed. The Triaging stage test asks whether the case carries large amounts of positive change forces; seven quantified forward drivers answer that directly, so the case clears the bar Triaging actually sets. Progression is explicitly a research decision, not a buy decision. Named condition: the Early-Stage Assessment is to be written after the Q3 2026 trading update in late October 2026, not before, because that print resolves the single most load-bearing uncertainty. Named trigger to reverse: if footwear growth stays below 2% currency-neutral for a second consecutive quarter while operating expenses again outgrow sales, the correct action becomes park, not progress. The risks report's own recommendation is adopted in full on capital and rejected only on stage progression.
case: The change forces are dense, named and largely contracted rather than aspirational. Internally: the supervisory board extended Bjorn Gulden's contract on 4 March 2026 to 31 December 2030, and he previously grew Puma sales from EUR 2,985m to EUR 8,465m. The footwear supply base was re-consolidated from 2024 with a new tier-one partner building dedicated vertically integrated Indonesian compounds and flexible smart-cell assembly lines; that partner's share of adidas volume is modelled from 1% in 2025 to 10% by 2028. Manufacturer cost structures were decoded with machine learning to force competitive bidding, which Jefferies expects to lift gross margin by about 100 basis points. Direct-to-consumer reached 43% of sales growing 25% currency-neutral. Performance running has scaled to a EUR 2.0bn to EUR 2.5bn business growing about 30%, with the Hyperboost platform launched commercially on 1 May 2026 at EUR 200 for the high-end model. The operating model was decentralised, with 500 headquarters roles removed, about 9% of the 5,800-person site.

Externally, the single largest force is a competitor in active retreat. Nike terminates online sales rights for Chinese wholesale distributors from 1 January 2027, and adidas is named the single largest near-term beneficiary; distributors including Topsports are expected to reallocate shelf space and marketing capital, replacing Nike volumes that historically generated 22% of Topsports' group revenue. Nike's Greater China revenue fell 17% currency-neutral and its regional share fell from 27% in 2020 to 16% in 2025; adidas recorded 10% Greater China retail share in 2025 with online sales up 32%. A February 2026 Supreme Court ruling voided certain emergency-powers tariffs, and refund claims of USD 250m to USD 300m sit outside guidance as a contingent asset, with a first small refund already recognised in the second quarter. Transactional currency effects are modelled to turn positive for gross margin into 2027, with hedges locked between 1.15 and 1.20 against the dollar. The market itself compounds at 4%, from USD 420bn in 2025 toward USD 500bn by 2028, against 1% for general apparel.

The base is cheap and well-invested even where it is not clean. The forward multiple of 12.5x sits at the 3rd percentile of its own ten-year range, and Deutsche Bank and Jefferies independently frame the stock at about 13x calendar-2027 earnings. The infrastructure is stated to support a EUR 30bn business against roughly EUR 26bn of revenue, so capital intensity can stay low. Delivery congruency supports the change thesis: nine profit beats and two in-line prints in twelve quarters before the second quarter of 2026, and every full period on record beat its initial operating-profit guide. Legacy stock was cleared for EUR 750m in 2023 and EUR 650m in 2024 without material write-offs, and gross margin recovered 785 basis points from 44.65% in the fourth quarter of 2023 to 52.5%.
counter_case: The risks report's own recommendation, quoted in the memo verbatim: "we recommend a hold-and-watch approach rather than immediate deployment of capital"; and its final tactical verdict, "we pass on the investment until the margin dilution from tournament opex is completely reversed". It records the aggregated failure probability as medium and notes that "the investment has a high likelihood of underperforming if opex growth continues to outpace revenue gains". The memo adopts both statements in full on capital and disagrees only on whether the case is worth further analytical work before the October print, on three grounds: the 3rd-percentile entry multiple, a dated resolution point in late October 2026, and the risks report's own re-run trigger, which is a monitoring instruction rather than a stop instruction.

The false friend is the central structural charge and it is the risks report's winning hypothesis. Its competing-hypotheses matrix scores the false-friend profile at zero logical inconsistencies against seven for the bull case and five for the bear. The diagnostics: footwear grew 1% currency-neutral while apparel grew 35%, a 3,400 basis-point divergence described as the widest in modern reporting history; apparel and jersey sales carry structurally lower gross margins than mature footwear lines, so the growth mix dilutes forward margin; operating expenses grew 17% against 14% currency-neutral sales growth, producing negative operating leverage in a record quarter; inventory reached 180% of next-quarter cost of goods sold with working capital at 24.0% of sales against 20.7%; lifestyle grew only 2% currency-neutral, and 30% to 40% of Originals footwear revenue sits in a franchise experts call at cycle end. Industry experts expect the retro terrace trend to lose market relevance by 2027, and Stan Smith and Superstar offer limited near-term volume replacement.
triggers: Eight key questions carried to the next stage. One, does second-half operating-overhead leverage appear, measured against the 29.9% first-half overhead ratio and 12% quarterly overhead growth. Two, does footwear growth recover above 2% currency-neutral, the level the risks report names as the trigger to re-run its pre-mortem. Three, does inventory normalise, with operating working capital returning toward 20.7% of sales from 24.0%. Four, how much of the USD 250m to USD 300m tariff refund is actually recovered and in which reporting periods it lands. Five, what replaces terrace volumes, given 30% to 40% of Originals footwear revenue sits in the rolling franchise. Six, does the transactional currency turn arrive, given hedges locked at 1.15 to 1.20 and option decay below 1.10. Seven, is the USD 8.7bn net dollar sourcing deficit a permanent structural feature and how far the 24-month hedge horizon protects gross margin. Eight, does the thin second-level management bench represent a real execution risk given the chief financial officer transition on 1 January 2027.

Timeline and sequencing. The Q3 2026 trading update in late October 2026 is the first observable resolution point, preceded by a September 2026 head-office analyst event. The Early-Stage Assessment should be written after the October print, not before. All five family reports are current to 11 August 2026, so no re-reading of the source set is required before the print; the next stage needs only a post-print earnings review.

Park triggers, if parking is chosen instead. Two consecutive quarters of footwear growth below 2% currency-neutral would confirm terminal saturation. Operating expenses growing faster than sales for a second consecutive quarter would convert the cost step-up from cyclical to structural. Operating working capital above 24.0% of sales at the year-end print would confirm a demand-forecasting failure rather than a tournament build. Watchlist placement would be a EUR 145 review level, near the 100-day average of EUR 158 and above the 52-week low.

Conviction movers. Conviction rises to high on a second-half overhead ratio below 29.9% combined with footwear growth above 2%, which would resolve both fulcrum drivers at once. Conviction falls to low on a second consecutive quarter of operating expenses outgrowing sales. Re-activation from park would require a rebased company guidance number combined with a full sell-side estimate reset, which together would complete the clearing setup the memo grades as half-formed.

Monitoring thresholds carried from source. Direct-to-consumer growth below 10% is a warning level against an expected 20% to 25%. Inventory cover expansion above 13% is a warning level, measured semi-annually. Wholesale pre-orders below 4% expansion is a warning level against an expected 6% to 7%. A euro-dollar rate below 1.10 is the hedge break point. Cadence proposed: quarterly on the two fulcrum drivers, semi-annually on inventory cover days and wholesale pre-orders.

Carve-out for the next stage. Two setups deepen at Early-Stage Assessment: the huge change-from-current clearing event in solid quality as primary, and the strong corporate change-driven earnings upgrade as secondary, the latter live on five of nine corporate deltas covering shareholder returns, strategy change, standards improvement and leadership changes, with the chief-executive delta three and a half years old and mergers and acquisitions absent. The false-friend guardrail becomes the primary invalidation test.
